cadpick:aef_t2_authorizations_first_tran: Indicates a carbon credit has received a formal government approval (authorization) classifying it by when that approval takes effect — at initial issuance, first cross-border transfer, or retirement.
The authorization point is triggered when the carbon credit crosses a national border for the first time; the host country's approval is recorded at that moment.
The authorization is granted at the moment the carbon credit is created (issued), so it arrives pre-approved for international use.
The authorization is only confirmed when the credit is actually used toward a climate target or permanently retired, not before.
cadpick:aef_t2_authorizations_metric.GHG: The authorization covers greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions or removals, measured in tonnes of CO2-equivalent.
cadpick:aef_t2_authorizations_metric.Non: The authorization covers outcomes not measured in greenhouse gas units — for example, biodiversity credits or water quality improvements.
cadpick:aef_t2_authorizations_purposes_f: The credit is authorized solely for Independent Market Purposes (IMP) — voluntary corporate carbon claims — not for counting toward a country's national climate target.
The credit is authorized to count toward a country's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) — its Paris Agreement climate pledge — requiring a corresponding adjustment so it is not double-counted.
The credit is dual-authorized: it can count toward a country's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and also be used for voluntary corporate climate claims (Independent Market Purposes).

The credit is authorized both for a country's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and for Other International Mitigation Purposes (OIMP) — uses outside voluntary corporate markets but not strictly NDC accounting.
The credit is authorized to contribute to a country's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and to Other Purposes (OP), a catch-all category beyond the standard voluntary and NDC uses.
The credit is authorized exclusively for Other International Mitigation Purposes (OIMP) — climate uses that are international but not a country's Paris Agreement NDC commitment.
The credit is authorized for Other Purposes (OP) only — uses that don't fit NDC accounting or standard voluntary-market claims.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_mitigation_type.E: The mitigation action cuts the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere — for example, switching from coal to solar power.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_mitigation_type.R: The mitigation action actively pulls greenhouse gases out of the atmosphere — for example, planting forests or direct air capture.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.Acquisition: A registry transaction where a party takes ownership of carbon credits, typically by purchasing them from another holder.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.Authorizatio: A government formally approves a carbon credit for a specific purpose (NDC accounting or voluntary markets), recorded as a distinct registry action.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.Cancellation: A carbon credit is permanently removed from circulation without being used toward any climate claim — for example, to avoid double use.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.First Transf: The first time a carbon credit moves across an international border, triggering Article 6 Paris Agreement accounting rules in the registry.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.Transfer: A carbon credit moves from one account to another within or across registries, without this being the first cross-border move.
cadpick:aef_t3_actions_type.Use: A carbon credit is applied toward a specific climate goal — such as a corporate net-zero claim — consuming it for that purpose.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 1 - No poverty: Flags that the carbon project contributes to UN Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1) by helping lift people out of extreme poverty as a side benefit beyond emission reductions.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 10 - Reduced i: Flags that the project delivers SDG 10 co-benefits by narrowing economic or social gaps between groups or regions, alongside its climate impact.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 11 - Sustainab: Flags SDG 11 co-benefits: the project improves urban infrastructure, housing, or resilience, making cities more sustainable alongside cutting emissions.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 12 - Responsib: Flags SDG 12 co-benefits: the project promotes sustainable resource use or waste reduction beyond its direct carbon impact.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 13 - Climate a: Flags SDG 13 co-benefits: the project directly advances climate resilience or adaptation efforts in addition to the quantified emission reductions.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 14 - Life belo: Flags SDG 14 co-benefits: the project protects or restores marine and coastal ecosystems — such as seagrass or mangroves — alongside its carbon accounting.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 15 - Life on l: Flags SDG 15 co-benefits: the project conserves or restores terrestrial biodiversity and ecosystems as a benefit beyond its emission reductions.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 16 - Peace and: Flags SDG 16 co-benefits: the project strengthens governance, rule of law, or community land rights as a side benefit of the climate activity.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 17 - Partnersh: Flags SDG 17 co-benefits: the project builds international cooperation or public-private partnerships that extend beyond the climate activity itself.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 2 - Zero hunge: Flags SDG 2 co-benefits: the project improves food security or supports sustainable agriculture as a benefit alongside its emission reductions.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 3 - Good healt: Flags SDG 3 co-benefits: the project improves community health outcomes — such as cleaner air from replacing dirty cookstoves — beyond its climate impact.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 4 - Quality ed: Flags SDG 4 co-benefits: the project generates revenue or capacity that funds or improves educational access in the host community.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 5 - Gender equ: Flags SDG 5 co-benefits: the project actively promotes women's participation, leadership, or economic empowerment alongside its climate work.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 6 - Clean wate: Flags SDG 6 co-benefits: the project improves access to safe drinking water or sanitation facilities in the project community.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 7 - Affordable: Flags SDG 7 co-benefits: the project expands access to affordable, reliable, clean energy — for example, solar mini-grids in off-grid communities.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 8 - Decent wor: Flags SDG 8 co-benefits: the project creates jobs or supports local economic growth as a community benefit beyond the carbon reduction.
cadpick:co_benefit_id.SDG 9 - Industry,: Flags SDG 9 co-benefits: the project builds local infrastructure or spurs innovation and industrial development alongside climate mitigation.
cadpick:label_type.Article 6 - Authorisa: A formal document from a host-country government authorizing a carbon credit under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement for international transfer or specific climate uses.
cadpick:label_type.Article 6 - Endorseme: A lighter-touch government statement supporting a carbon project under Article 6 without the full legal weight of a formal authorization.
cadpick:label_type.Article 6 - Letter of: Official written approval from a host country confirming a project meets national requirements and may proceed under Article 6 Paris Agreement rules.
A government-issued letter confirming that a carbon project qualifies for Article 6 international carbon market participation, often a prerequisite for authorization.
cadpick:label_type.Certification: A third-party or standard-body certificate confirming the project meets a recognized carbon standard's requirements — such as Verra VCS or Gold Standard.

cadpick:project_sector.Agriculture, fore: Carbon project falls under agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU), the sector covering emissions and removals from land management and livestock.
cadpick:project_sector.Any combination o: Carbon project spans multiple sectors listed elsewhere in this picklist, rather than fitting a single category.
cadpick:project_sector.Carbon capture an: Carbon project captures carbon dioxide directly from industrial sources or the atmosphere and stores it underground or in long-lived materials to prevent atmospheric release.

cadpick:project_sector.Construction: Carbon project reduces emissions from the construction sector, for example through low-carbon building materials, energy-efficient design, or construction process improvements.

cadpick:project_sector.Energy distributi: Carbon project reduces losses or emissions in energy distribution networks, such as reducing gas pipeline leaks or improving electricity grid efficiency.
cadpick:project_sector.Energy industries: Carbon project relates to power generation, either expanding renewable energy capacity or improving efficiency of conventional power plants to lower per-unit emissions.
cadpick:project_sector.Fugitive emission: Carbon project reduces unintended greenhouse gas leaks from coal mining, oil extraction, or natural gas handling and distribution infrastructure.

cadpick:project_sector.Livestock and man: Carbon project reduces methane and nitrous oxide emissions from livestock digestion (enteric fermentation) or the storage and treatment of animal manure.
cadpick:project_sector.Manufacturing ind: Carbon project reduces greenhouse gas emissions from manufacturing facilities, such as cement, glass, or paper production.
cadpick:project_sector.Metal production: Carbon project reduces emissions from the smelting or refining of metals such as steel, aluminium, or copper.
cadpick:project_sector.Mining/mineral pr: Carbon project reduces greenhouse gas emissions from extracting or processing minerals and raw materials.
cadpick:project_sector.Others: Carbon project does not fit any of the standard sector categories and falls under a miscellaneous or unlisted sector.
cadpick:project_sector.Solvent use: Carbon project reduces emissions of volatile organic compounds or greenhouse gases from industrial or commercial solvent applications.
cadpick:project_sector.Transport: Carbon project reduces greenhouse gas emissions from transportation, such as fuel switching, vehicle efficiency improvements, or modal shifts.
cadpick:project_sector.Urban Development: Carbon project focuses on low-carbon urban planning or infrastructure, such as green buildings, public transit, or sustainable city design.
cadpick:project_sector.Waste handling an: A carbon project whose primary activity is managing waste streams — landfills, sewage, composting — to cut greenhouse gas emissions from decomposing organic material.
cadpick:project_status.Certified: A carbon project that has passed all required audits and been awarded a certificate by its standard body, confirming the emission reductions are genuine.
cadpick:project_status.Completed: A carbon project whose crediting period has ended and no further carbon credits will be generated, though existing credits remain valid.
cadpick:project_status.Inactive: A carbon project that is no longer generating credits and is not actively progressing through the registration or verification pipeline.
cadpick:project_status.Listed: A carbon project formally entered on a registry's public listing, making it discoverable but not yet registered or verified.
cadpick:project_status.Registered: A carbon project accepted onto a standard's registry after meeting baseline eligibility requirements, allowing credit issuance to proceed.
cadpick:project_status.Rejected: A project application that was refused by the standard or registry body, meaning no credits will be issued under this submission.
cadpick:project_status.Validated: A carbon project whose design document has been independently reviewed by a third party and confirmed to meet the standard's methodology requirements.
cadpick:project_status.Verified: A carbon project whose actual emission reductions have been measured and confirmed by an independent auditor, clearing them for credit issuance.
cadpick:project_status.Withdrawn: A project voluntarily removed from a registry by its developer before or during the registration process, forfeiting any pending credits.
cadpick:project_type.Afforestation: A carbon project that plants trees on land not forested for at least a decade, creating new forest cover that absorbs carbon dioxide.
cadpick:project_type.Agriculture: A carbon project reducing emissions from farming practices — such as improved rice cultivation, livestock management, or soil carbon sequestration.
cadpick:project_type.Any combination of: A carbon project spanning multiple activity types (e.g., forestry plus renewable energy) bundled into a single registered program.
cadpick:project_type.Biogas: A carbon project capturing methane-rich gas from organic waste — manure, food waste, or sewage — and using it as energy instead of releasing it to the atmosphere.
cadpick:project_type.Biomass Energy: A carbon project generating electricity or heat from plant-based materials (wood, agricultural residues) that displace fossil fuels.
cadpick:project_type.CO2 usage: A carbon project that captures carbon dioxide and puts it to productive use — for example, in manufacturing materials — rather than releasing it as a gas.
cadpick:project_type.Cement: A carbon project cutting emissions from cement production, typically by replacing clinker with less carbon-intensive materials or capturing process emissions.
cadpick:project_type.Coal bed/mine metha: A carbon project capturing methane leaking from coal seams or active mines, preventing a potent greenhouse gas from venting to the atmosphere.
cadpick:project_type.Energy Efficiency I: A carbon project that reduces energy consumption in industrial facilities — factories, smelters, refineries — through upgraded equipment or processes.
cadpick:project_type.Energy Efficiency h: A carbon project that cuts household energy use through measures such as efficient cookstoves, insulation, or LED lighting.
cadpick:project_type.Energy Efficiency o: A carbon project where an organisation improves the efficiency of its own power or heat generation, reducing the fuel burned per unit of output.
cadpick:project_type.Energy Efficiency s: A carbon project improving energy efficiency in commercial or public-service buildings — offices, hospitals, schools — reducing grid electricity demand.
A carbon project that reduces losses in electricity transmission and distribution networks so that more power reaches end-users per unit generated.
cadpick:project_type.Energy distribution: A carbon project focused on improving energy delivery infrastructure — grids or pipelines — to reduce transmission losses and associated emissions.
cadpick:project_type.Fossil fuel switch: A carbon project replacing a high-carbon fuel (coal, oil) with a lower-carbon one (natural gas, bioenergy) in an existing facility.
cadpick:project_type.Fugitive: A carbon project preventing unintentional greenhouse gas leaks from oil and gas equipment, refrigeration systems, or industrial processes.
cadpick:project_type.Geothermal: A carbon project generating clean electricity or heat by tapping natural geothermal energy from the earth, displacing fossil-fuel power.
cadpick:project_type.Hydro: A carbon project generating emission-free electricity from flowing or falling water, displacing fossil-fuel generation on the grid.
cadpick:project_type.Landfill gas: A carbon project capturing methane produced as buried waste decomposes in a landfill, then burning or using it rather than letting it escape.
cadpick:project_type.Methane avoidance: A carbon project preventing methane from forming or escaping — for example, by covering manure lagoons — rather than capturing it after release.
cadpick:project_type.N2O: A carbon project reducing nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, typically from agricultural fertilisers or industrial chemical processes.
cadpick:project_type.PFCs and SF6: A carbon project cutting perfluorocarbons (PFCs) and sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) — extremely potent industrial greenhouse gases used in electronics and electrical equipment.
cadpick:project_type.Reforestation: A carbon project restoring forest cover on land that was previously deforested, allowing trees to reabsorb carbon dioxide over time.
cadpick:project_type.Solar: A carbon project generating electricity from sunlight via photovoltaic panels or solar thermal systems, replacing fossil-fuel power.
cadpick:project_type.Tidal: A carbon project harnessing tidal or wave energy to generate clean electricity, displacing grid power from fossil fuels.
cadpick:project_type.Transport: A carbon project reducing emissions from moving people or goods — through fuel switching, efficiency gains, or modal shift to lower-carbon options.
cadpick:project_type.Waste: A carbon project reducing greenhouse gas emissions from solid waste management — diverting material from landfill, improving composting, or recovering energy.
cadpick:project_type.Wind: A carbon project generating electricity from wind turbines, displacing fossil-fuel generation and producing no direct emissions during operation.

cadpick:project_unit_metric.kt (Kiloton): Kiloton — a unit equal to one thousand metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, used to express large volumes of emission reductions.
cadpick:project_unit_metric.tCO2e: Tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) — the standard unit for carbon credits, where one tCO2e represents one metric tonne of greenhouse gases expressed as CO2.

cadpick:stakeholder_type.Consultant: A professional adviser hired by a carbon project — such as a methodology expert or carbon accountant — who is not the project owner or developer.
cadpick:stakeholder_type.Developer: The organisation or individual that designs, implements, and manages a carbon project to generate emission reductions.
cadpick:stakeholder_type.Owner: The entity that holds legal title to a carbon project or the land and assets on which it operates.
cadpick:unit_status.Buffer: A carbon credit held in a reserve pool, set aside to cover the risk that future emission reductions do not materialise — not available to buyers.
cadpick:unit_status.Cancelled: A carbon credit permanently removed from circulation — for example, due to a project integrity problem — making it unusable for offsetting purposes.
cadpick:unit_status.Expired: A carbon credit that has passed its validity date without being retired, rendering it no longer eligible to offset emissions.
cadpick:unit_status.Held: A carbon credit that has been issued and is held in an account but has not yet been transferred to a buyer or retired against an emission claim.
cadpick:unit_status.Inactive: A carbon credit account or block that is not currently available for trading or retirement, often pending administrative action.
cadpick:unit_status.Issued: A carbon credit officially created by a registry following independent verification of emission reductions, now available for sale or retirement.
cadpick:unit_status.Rejected: A carbon credit application refused by the registry or standard body, meaning no tradeable credit is created from the underlying emission reduction.
cadpick:unit_status.Retired: A carbon credit permanently removed from the market by a buyer to claim an offset against their own emissions — it cannot be resold or reused.
cadpick:unit_type.Avoidance - nature: A credit representing greenhouse gas emissions prevented through nature-based means, such as protecting forests that would otherwise be cleared.
cadpick:unit_type.Avoidance - technical: A credit representing greenhouse gas emissions prevented through engineered interventions, such as capturing landfill methane or switching fossil fuels.
cadpick:unit_type.Not Determined: A credit whose type — avoidance, reduction, or removal — has not yet been classified in the registry record.
cadpick:unit_type.Reduction - nature: A credit representing a measurable decrease in greenhouse gas emissions achieved through nature-based practices such as improved land management or agroforestry.
cadpick:unit_type.Reduction - technical: A credit representing a measurable decrease in greenhouse gas emissions achieved through technology or process improvements, such as energy efficiency upgrades.
cadpick:unit_type.Removal - nature: A credit representing carbon dioxide actively drawn from the atmosphere and stored through natural processes such as tree growth or soil carbon sequestration.
cadpick:unit_type.Removal - technical: A credit representing carbon dioxide actively removed from the atmosphere through engineered processes such as direct air capture or bioenergy with carbon capture.
cadpick:validation_type.Validation of Po: A third-party audit confirming that a material change made to a carbon project after initial registration still meets the applicable standard's requirements.
cadpick:validation_type.Validation of Pr: A third-party audit of a carbon project's design document, confirming the proposed methodology and baseline calculations meet the standard before crediting begins.
cadpick:validation_type.Validation of Re: A third-party audit confirming a carbon project remains eligible to generate credits during a renewed crediting period, verifying the baseline and additionality still hold.

comet:Material.materialId: A globally recognized product identifier such as a GTIN barcode or CAS chemical number, uniquely pinpointing the material.

comet:TimePeriod.startDate: The opening date and time of the reporting or monitoring interval.
comet:UnitOfMeasure: A standardized quantity unit (e.g., kilogram, megajoule, tonne CO2e) drawn from the W3C QUDT vocabulary, used to express measured values.
comet-cn:Additional: A carbon credit criterion picklist value indicating that the credited emission reduction would not have occurred without the incentive provided by the carbon project (additionality).

comet-cn:BasePeriod: The historical reference period (per ISO 14068-1 §3.2.14) against which a company compares all later reporting periods to measure emission progress.
comet-cn:Baseline: The quantified greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and/or removals of a subject during the base period (per ISO 14068-1 §3.2.13), serving as the reference level for measuring reductions.
comet-cn:CarbonNeutralityClaim: A public declaration that a subject has achieved carbon neutrality (per ISO 14068-1 §3.1.3), valid only when all preceding steps — commitment, plan, reductions, offsetting, and verification — are documented.
comet-cn:CarbonNeutralityCommitment: A formal top-management statement (per ISO 14068-1 §6) establishing the scope, governance, and improvement obligations for pursuing carbon neutrality — required before any neutrality claim can be made.
comet-cn:CarbonNeutralityManagementPlan: The structured document (per ISO 14068-1 §9) containing the organization's baseline, reduction pathway, interim targets, planned credits, and monitoring indicators for achieving carbon neutrality.
comet-cn:CarbonNeutralityPathway: A time-stamped trajectory (per ISO 14068-1 §5.3) showing short- and long-term emission reduction targets, ideally aligned to a science-based pathway, leading to a target year with only residual emissions remaining.
comet-cn:CarbonNeutralityReport: The publicly disclosed annual report (per ISO 14068-1 §12) that documents the subject's footprint, reduction progress, credit retirements, corresponding adjustments, and independent verification opinion.
comet-cn:Certified: A carbon credit quality criterion indicating the credit has been independently verified and issued under a recognized crediting programme.
comet-cn:CorrespondingAdjustment: An accounting entry (per Paris Agreement Article 6.4) that prevents double-counting by ensuring a credit used by a private company is simultaneously deducted from the host country's national climate contribution (NDC).
comet-cn:CreditCriterion: One of five mandatory quality tests (per ISO 14068-1 §11.2) a carbon credit must pass — Real, Additional, Measurable, Permanent, Certified — before it can be used in a carbon neutrality claim.
comet-cn:CreditType: The classification of a tradeable carbon credit by its mitigation method (per ISO 14068-1 §3.3.2 Note 2), distinguishing avoidance, reduction, and removal credits.
comet-cn:CreditingProgrammeCriterion: A programme-level requirement (per ISO 14068-1 §11.3) a crediting scheme must satisfy — including transparent governance, stakeholder consultation, independent verification, and a public registry with serial numbers.
comet-cn:Enhance_Removal_Inside_Boundary: A carbon neutrality hierarchy action option indicating the entity will increase carbon removals within its own operational boundary (e.g., planting trees on company land).
comet-cn:Entity: The organization (per ISO 14068-1 §3.4.1) that is pursuing and declaring carbon neutrality for a specific subject, which may be itself or one of its products.
comet-cn:FinancedEmissionsAccount: The share of an investee's carbon footprint attributable to a financial institution's lending or investment exposure (per ISO 14068-1 Annex B.3), calculated using the PCAF methodology.
comet-cn:FinancialInstitution: A regulated bank, insurer, or investment firm (per ISO 14068-1 §3.4.3.1) subject to additional ISO 14068-1 requirements covering emissions from its loan and investment portfolio.
comet-cn:GHGEmissionReduction: A measured decrease in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions within the subject's boundary relative to a baseline or earlier point in time (per ISO 14068-1 §3.2.3); distinct from purchasing offset credits.
comet-cn:GHGRemovalEnhancement: A measured increase in carbon removals within the subject's boundary relative to a baseline (per ISO 14068-1 §3.2.8); any subsequent reversal must be re-recorded as an emission.
comet-cn:HierarchyAction: One of three mandatory steps (per ISO 14068-1 §4.4) an entity must follow in priority order: first reduce emissions inside the boundary, then enhance removals inside the boundary, and only then offset with external credits.
comet-cn:Measurable: A carbon credit quality criterion indicating the credited emission reduction or removal can be quantified using an approved methodology.
comet-cn:Offset_Outside_Boundary: The third and lowest-priority hierarchy action — purchasing and retiring carbon credits from projects outside the entity's boundary to compensate for remaining emissions.
comet-cn:OffsettingEvent: The act of retiring qualifying carbon credits against a reported carbon footprint (per ISO 14068-1 §3.3.1), which must occur in a public registry within 12 months of the reporting period's close.
comet-cn:Permanent: A carbon credit quality criterion indicating the credited emission reduction or removal will not be reversed over time.
comet-cn:Principle: A foundational governing principle of the ISO 14068-1 carbon neutrality standard that overarches all requirements.
comet-cn:Real: A carbon credit quality criterion indicating the credited emission reduction or removal has actually occurred and is not hypothetical.
comet-cn:Reduce_Inside_Boundary: The highest-priority hierarchy action — cutting actual greenhouse gas emissions from the entity's own operations before resorting to offsets.
comet-cn:ReductionCredit: A carbon credit representing a verified reduction in greenhouse gas emissions achieved by a project (e.g., installing efficient cookstoves).
comet-cn:RemovalCredit: A carbon credit representing verified removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere (e.g., afforestation or direct air capture).
comet-cn:RemovalReversal: A previously claimed in-boundary carbon removal that has been lost (per ISO 14068-1 §10.2), such as a forest burned down; must be re-recorded as an emission in the period the loss occurred.
comet-cn:ReportingPeriod: The specific historical timeframe, typically one calendar year, for which a carbon neutrality determination is made (per ISO 14068-1 §3.1.6).
comet-cn:ResidualGHGEmission: Greenhouse gas emissions that remain after a company or product has applied every technically and economically feasible reduction measure. Under ISO 14068-1, only these irreducible leftovers may be offset to complete a carbon-neutrality claim.
comet-cn:Subject: The specific organisation or product for which a carbon-neutrality claim is being made. It defines what is being measured, what reductions are tracked, and whose name appears on the published claim.
comet-cn:UnabatedGHGEmission: All greenhouse gas emissions remaining after reduction actions within an organisation's or product's boundary — a broader category than residual emissions because not all feasible reductions may have been applied yet.
comet-cn:VerificationOpinion: The formal written statement from an independent third-party verifier confirming that a carbon-neutrality report meets ISO 14068-1 and ISO 14064-3 requirements. Required before a claim can be published.
comet-cn:correspondingAdjustmentApplied: A true/false flag on a carbon credit indicating whether the host country has made the accounting adjustment required under Paris Agreement Article 6 so the reduction cannot be counted twice.
comet-cn:hasBaseline: Links a carbon-neutrality management plan to the reference emissions baseline from which reductions are measured.
comet-cn:hasBoundary: Links the subject of a carbon-neutrality claim to the scope boundary defining which emission sources are included.
comet-cn:hasClaim: Links an organisation to the carbon-neutrality claim it has published.
comet-cn:hasCommitment: Links a carbon-neutrality management plan to the formal commitment (target, timeline, and actions) the organisation has made.
comet-cn:hasCreditType: Links a carbon credit to its classification — for example, removal versus reduction, or nature-based versus technology-based.
comet-cn:hasPathway: Links a carbon-neutrality management plan to the decarbonisation trajectory the organisation is following toward its target year.
comet-cn:hasReport: Links a carbon-neutrality claim to the supporting report that documents the methodology, data, and results behind it.
comet-cn:hasReportingPeriod: Links a record to the calendar window (start and end dates) for which emissions data were collected and reported.
comet-cn:hasSubject: Links an entity record to the organisation or product that is the subject of the carbon-neutrality claim.
comet-cn:hasVerificationOpinion: Links a carbon-neutrality report to the independent verification statement that confirms its validity.
comet-cn:hierarchyStep: Links a record to a specific action in the mitigation hierarchy — reduce first, then offset — indicating where in that ordered sequence an action sits.
comet-cn:isExPostCredit: A true/false flag confirming that a carbon credit represents reductions or removals that have already happened. ISO 14068 requires credits used in neutrality claims to be ex-post (verified after the fact), not forward-looking.
comet-cn:meetsCriterion: Links a carbon credit to a specific quality criterion — such as additionality or permanence — that the credit satisfies under ISO 14068.
comet-cn:reportingPeriodEnd: The closing date of the period covered by a carbon-neutrality report or disclosure.
comet-cn:reportingPeriodStart: The opening date of the period covered by a carbon-neutrality report or disclosure.
comet-cn:retirementDate: The date a carbon credit was permanently cancelled to support a neutrality claim. ISO 14068 requires retirement within 12 months of the reporting period end.
comet-cn:targetYearResidualOnly: The year — commonly 2050 — by which an organisation plans to have cut emissions so far that only irreducible residual emissions remain, marking the long-term anchor of its decarbonisation pathway.
comet-cn:vintageEndYear: The last year of the period during which a carbon credit's emission reductions occurred. ISO 14068 requires this to be no more than five years before the start of the neutrality claim period.
comet-eac:Article6Authorization: Formal approval from a host country allowing an internationally transferred mitigation outcome (ITMO) under Paris Agreement Article 6 to be used by another country or entity for their climate targets.
comet-eac:Article6Holdings: A registry account showing the current balance of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) held by a country or authorised participant under Paris Agreement Article 6.
comet-eac:Article6Transfer: A recorded transaction moving internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) from one country's registry account to another under Paris Agreement Article 6.
comet-eac:BookAndClaim: A chain-of-custody model in which the physical product and its environmental attribute are traded separately, so a buyer can claim the attribute without physically receiving the associated commodity.
comet-eac:CORSIAEligibleUnit: A carbon offset unit approved by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Technical Advisory Body for use by airlines under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).
comet-eac:CORSIAEligibleUnit.eligiblePer: The specific CORSIA compliance phase and vintage window during which a unit qualifies for use by airlines under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation.
comet-eac:CarbonRemovalCert: An environmental attribute certificate representing verified removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, covering technology types such as direct air capture (DAC), biochar, and bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS).
comet-eac:CertificateRegistry: The official platform that issues, tracks, and retires environmental attribute certificates, ensuring no double-counting across buyers.
comet-eac:CertificateRegistry.programNam: The name of the crediting or verification program (e.g., Gold Standard, Verra VCS) under whose rules a registry issues certificates.
comet-eac:CertificateRegistry.registryNa: The name of the specific database or platform (e.g., Markit, APX) where certificate serial numbers and transaction records are held.
comet-eac:CoBenefit: An additional social or environmental benefit beyond carbon reduction that a project delivers, typically aligned with one of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) such as clean water or biodiversity.
comet-eac:EAC: An environmental attribute certificate (EAC) — a tradeable instrument that conveys the non-carbon or carbon attributes of one unit of energy or emission reduction, separate from the underlying commodity.
comet-eac:EAC.chainOfCustody: The tracking model used to follow an environmental attribute certificate from its point of origin through all transfers to the final buyer — for example, mass balance or physical segregation.
comet-eac:EAC.issueDate: The date the registry created and assigned a serial number to an environmental attribute certificate.
comet-eac:EAC.registry: The name of the registry that issued a particular environmental attribute certificate.
comet-eac:EAC.serialNumber: The unique identifier assigned by a registry to an individual environmental attribute certificate, used to track and prevent double-counting.
comet-eac:EAC.unitCount: The number of credits or attribute units represented by a certificate, typically measured in megawatt-hours of energy or tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
comet-eac:EAC.unitStatus: The current lifecycle stage of a certificate — for example, issued, transferred, or retired — as recorded in the registry.
comet-eac:EAC.unitType: The category of environmental benefit a certificate represents: avoided emissions, reduced emissions, or carbon removal; and whether the project uses natural or technology-based methods.
comet-eac:EAC.vintageYear: The calendar year in which the underlying emission reduction or renewable energy generation actually occurred.
comet-eac:EnergyAttributeCert: An environmental attribute certificate representing the renewable or low-carbon characteristics of electricity generation, such as an international renewable energy certificate (I-REC), guarantee of origin (GO), or renewable energy certificate (REC).
comet-eac:MaterialStewardCert: An environmental attribute certificate attesting that a material was produced according to responsible sourcing or sustainability standards, such as ResponsibleSteel or the Aluminium Stewardship Initiative (ASI).
comet-eac:RetirementEvent: The transaction record created when an environmental attribute certificate is permanently cancelled so its benefit can be claimed by a buyer and cannot be sold again.
comet-eac:RetirementEvent.retirementBene: The organisation on whose behalf an environmental attribute certificate was retired and whose sustainability claim the retirement supports.
comet-eac:RetirementEvent.retirementDate: The date a certificate was permanently cancelled in the registry, ending its tradeable life.
comet-ef:DataProvenance: A record of where an emission factor came from — which database, version, and methodology — so auditors can trace and verify the number used in a carbon calculation.
comet-ef:EmissionFactor: A coefficient that converts an activity quantity (e.g., litres of fuel or kWh of electricity) into an equivalent mass of greenhouse gas emissions, expressed in kg CO2e per unit of activity.
comet-ef:EmissionFactor.efGeography: The country or region for which an emission factor applies, coded to the ISO 3166 standard, since grid carbon intensity and industrial processes vary by location.
comet-ef:EmissionFactor.efSource: The name of the database or publication from which an emission factor was drawn, such as IPCC, ecoinvent, or a national government inventory.
comet-ef:EmissionFactor.efUnit: The unit denominator for an emission factor, such as kg CO2e per kilowatt-hour (kWh) or per tonne of material, needed to apply the factor correctly.
comet-ef:EmissionFactor.efValue: The numeric value of the emission factor — the actual coefficient used to multiply activity data and produce a greenhouse gas emission quantity.
comet-ef:GWP100Value: A global warming potential (GWP) value expressing how much heat a greenhouse gas traps relative to CO2 over a 100-year timeframe, used to convert gas-specific emissions into CO2-equivalent tonnes.
comet-ef:GWP100Value.gasSpecies: The specific greenhouse gas — such as CO2, methane (CH4), or nitrous oxide (N2O) — to which a GWP100 factor applies.
comet-ef:GWP100Value.gwpValue: The numeric GWP100 coefficient for a greenhouse gas — for example, methane has a GWP100 of about 28 under IPCC AR6 — used to convert it to CO2 equivalents.
comet-ef:GWP100Value.ipccAR: The IPCC Assessment Report edition (AR5 or AR6) whose GWP values are being used, since the coefficients differ between reports and regulators may specify which edition applies.
comet-ef:GeographyScope: The spatial coverage — country, region, or global — that an emission factor is representative of, affecting how accurately it reflects local conditions.
comet-ef:LCIDataset: A life cycle inventory (LCI) dataset containing the inputs, outputs, and associated emissions for a specific process or product, used as the source data for calculating an emission factor.
comet-ef:TechRepLevel: A score indicating how well an emission factor represents the actual technology in use — high representativeness means the factor matches the specific process; low means it is a generic approximation.
comet-mkt:CBAMShadowTariff: Estimated import duty exposure under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), calculated from embedded emissions multiplied by the gap between the EU carbon price and any carbon price already paid in the exporting country.
comet-mkt:CBAMShadowTariff.euETSPrice: The current price of an EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowance in euros per tonne of CO2 equivalent, used as the reference rate for calculating CBAM import duties.
comet-mkt:CBAMShadowTariff.thirdCountryC: The carbon price (in euros per tonne CO2e) already paid by a producer in the country of origin, which can be deducted from the CBAM duty to avoid double-charging.
comet-mkt:CarbonPremium: The extra price a buyer pays for a low-carbon product or service above the market rate for a conventional equivalent, reflecting the value placed on reduced emissions.
comet-mkt:CarbonPremium.premiumValue: The monetary amount of the price premium for a low-carbon product, expressed in a currency per unit of product.
comet-mkt:CleanHydrogenCreditTier: One of four tiers under the US Inflation Reduction Act Section 45V production tax credit, ranging from $0.60 to $3.00 per kilogram of hydrogen, where higher tiers require lower lifecycle carbon intensity.
comet-mkt:CleanHydrogenCreditTier.credit: The tax credit amount in US dollars per kilogram of qualified clean hydrogen that a producer receives under the IRA Section 45V tier classification.
comet-mkt:EACSpotPrice: The current market price for buying or selling an environmental attribute certificate (EAC) such as a renewable energy certificate or carbon offset, expressed per unit.
comet-mkt:MarketBenchmark: A reference price or performance index against which a carbon or environmental credit is compared, used to assess whether a price or intensity is above or below market norms.
comet-mkt:PricingSignal: Any carbon-related price — an emissions trading price, a carbon tax rate, or a credit market price — that signals the economic cost of greenhouse gas emissions to decision-makers.
comet-pcf:AllocationMethod: The rule used to divide shared emissions across multiple products from the same process, such as by mass, economic value, energy content, physical causality, or product category rules (PCR).
comet-pcf:BiogenicCarbon: Carbon dioxide absorbed from the atmosphere by plants and other living matter during growth, tracked separately from fossil emissions per ISO 14067 because it can re-enter or leave the carbon cycle.
comet-pcf:BiogenicCarbon.biogenicCarbonC: The mass of biogenic carbon stored within a product at the time of measurement, expressed in kg CO2 equivalent per unit.
comet-pcf:BiogenicCarbon.biogenicUptake: The CO2 drawn from the atmosphere by plant growth and temporarily stored in a biobased product, recorded as a negative (removal) in the product carbon footprint (PCF).
comet-pcf:BiogenicCarbon.landUseChange: Emissions caused by converting land from one use to another — for example, clearing forest for agriculture — attributed to biobased raw materials in a product's lifecycle.
comet-pcf:CBAMDeclaration: A formal declaration of the greenhouse gas emissions embedded in goods imported into the EU, required under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to calculate the import levy owed.
comet-pcf:CBAMDeclaration.cnCode: The eight-digit Combined Nomenclature (CN) customs code identifying the type of goods covered by a CBAM embedded-emissions declaration.
comet-pcf:CarbonIntensity: The amount of greenhouse gases emitted per unit of product over its full lifecycle, expressed in kg CO2 equivalent per kilogram or per megajoule, enabling comparison of competing products or production routes.
comet-pcf:CarbonIntensity.functionalBasi: The unit denominator — per kilogram, per megajoule, or per product unit — chosen to express carbon intensity, which must match the declared unit to allow valid comparison.
comet-pcf:EPDDeclaration: An environmental product declaration (EPD) produced according to the EN 15804 construction standard, disclosing a product's environmental impacts including its carbon footprint across defined lifecycle stages.
comet-pcf:EmbeddedEmissions: The total greenhouse gas emissions locked into an imported product per tonne of output, covering both direct plant emissions and electricity-related emissions, as required for CBAM reporting.
comet-pcf:EmbeddedEmissions.directEmissi: The Scope 1 (on-site combustion and process) emissions at the manufacturing installation per tonne of product, one of two components in a CBAM embedded-emissions calculation.
comet-pcf:EmbeddedEmissions.indirectEmis: The greenhouse gases attributed to purchased electricity consumed during manufacturing, expressed per tonne of product, forming the second component of CBAM embedded emissions.
comet-pcf:EmbeddedEmissions.productionRo: The manufacturing technology pathway used — such as basic oxygen furnace (BOF) or electric arc furnace (EAF) for steel — which determines the applicable emission calculation methodology.
comet-pcf:EmbeddedEmissions.specificEmbe: The combined total of direct and indirect embedded emissions per tonne of product, the final figure reported under CBAM to determine import duty exposure.
comet-pcf:FunctionalUnit: The precisely defined quantity of product or service that a carbon footprint refers to — for example, one tonne of steel coil — stated using standardised units so results from different studies can be compared.
comet-pcf:LCIAResult: The output of a lifecycle impact assessment (LCIA), quantifying a product's contribution to one or more environmental impact categories such as climate change, water use, or eutrophication.
comet-pcf:PCRReference: A citation to the product category rules (PCR) document that governed how a product carbon footprint (PCF) was calculated, ensuring results follow sector-specific calculation rules for comparability.
comet-pcf:ProductCarbonFootprint: The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by a product across its lifecycle, calculated per declared unit under ISO 14067 and expressed in kg CO2 equivalent.
comet-pcf:ProductCarbonFootprint.exempte: The share of a product's lifecycle inputs excluded from the footprint calculation under a cutoff rule — ISO 14067 limits this to a maximum of 5% of total mass and emissions.
comet-pcf:ProductCarbonFootprint.fossilG: The portion of a product's carbon footprint attributable exclusively to fossil fuel combustion and fossil-origin process emissions, expressed in kg CO2 equivalent per declared unit.
comet-pcf:ProductCarbonFootprint.pcfId: The unique identifier assigned to a specific product carbon footprint (PCF) record, used to reference it without ambiguity in data exchanges.
comet-pcf:ProductCarbonFootprint.totalGW: The complete carbon footprint of a product including both fossil and biogenic greenhouse gas contributions, expressed in kg CO2 equivalent per declared unit.
comet-pcf:StandardRef: A reference to the cross-sectoral methodology standard — such as ISO 14067 or the GHG Protocol Product Standard — used to calculate a product carbon footprint.
comet-pcf:SystemBoundary: The scope of lifecycle stages included in a carbon footprint calculation — for example, cradle-to-gate covers raw material extraction through factory gate, while cradle-to-grave extends to end-of-life disposal.
comet-pcf:UncertaintyAssessment: A quantified range expressing how much a carbon footprint result might vary due to data gaps, modelling assumptions, and measurement errors, helping users understand confidence in the number.
comet-pj:EcoLeafDeclaration: A Japanese environmental product declaration (EPD) issued under the SuMPO EcoLeaf program, disclosing the lifecycle environmental impacts of a product according to Japanese product category rules.
comet-pj:ISO21930PCR: A SuMPO product category rules (PCR) document aligned with ISO 21930, the international standard for environmental declarations of construction products, used to guide lifecycle assessment studies in Japan.
comet-pj:LegacyEcoLeafPCR: An older SuMPO product category rules (PCR) document registered before 2024, identified by the PA-NNNNNN-XX-NN numbering format rather than the current PA-SuMPO-PCR scheme.
comet-pj:SuMPOPCRDocument: A product category rules (PCR) document published by Japan's SuMPO environmental labelling program, setting calculation rules for a product type aligned with either ISO 21930 or EN 15804.
comet-pj:japanesePCRField: Links a SuMPO PCR document to its product field classification in the Japanese taxonomy of product categories, indicating which industry sector the PCR covers.
comet-pj:pcrOverviewJa: The Japanese-language scope description taken verbatim from a SuMPO PCR document, preserved as primary evidence of what product types and lifecycle stages the rules govern.
comet-pj:pcrRegistrationNumber: The official SuMPO reference number assigned to a product category rules (PCR) document, in either the legacy PA-NNNNNN-XX-NN format or the current PA-SuMPO-PCR-NNNNN format.
comet-pj:validityPeriodJa: The validity period of a SuMPO PCR document as stated in the original Japanese text, indicating when the rules expire and must be reviewed.
comet-pj:workingGroupMember: An organisation that participated in the expert working group that drafted a SuMPO PCR document, providing industry and technical expertise for the rules.
comet-rs:AmbitionGapAnalysis: A required analysis under ResponsibleSteel when a steelmaking site's actual emissions deviate from its published decarbonisation trajectory, documenting the gap, its causes, and the corrective actions planned.
comet-rs:AssurancePanelReview: An independent review by the ResponsibleSteel Assurance Panel of a certification body's audit report before any site certification decision is issued — a governance step unique to the ResponsibleSteel scheme.
comet-rs:BF_BOF: The conventional integrated steelmaking route combining a blast furnace (BF) to produce pig iron with a basic oxygen furnace (BOF) to convert it to steel — the most carbon-intensive mainstream production method.
comet-rs:CCUSCredit: A greenhouse gas emissions credit awarded to a steelmaking site for permanently storing captured process gases underground, reducing the site's reported emissions intensity after accounting for capture and transport energy.
comet-rs:CertificationAudit: A formal on-site assessment by a ResponsibleSteel-approved certification body covering all 13 Principles of the Production Standard, producing the audit report that goes to the Assurance Panel for review.
comet-rs:CertifiedSite: A steelmaking site that has achieved or is pursuing ResponsibleSteel certification, with its audit boundary and certification status tracked in the ontology alongside standard site properties.
comet-rs:CertifiedSteelMark: The product-level label that a ResponsibleSteel certified site may apply to its steel products, displaying the site's Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) and Sourcing Progress Level (SPL) ratings.
comet-rs:CoCClaim: An assertion by a downstream manufacturer or buyer that a product contains or was made with ResponsibleSteel certified steel, backed by a documented chain of custody transfer trail.
comet-rs:CoCTransferEvent: A recorded handover of ResponsibleSteel certified steel from one supply chain participant to the next, documenting quantity, product type, parties, date, and the chain of custody (CoC) model used.
comet-rs:CoreSiteCertification: The base level of ResponsibleSteel certification, confirming a steelmaking site meets all mandatory criteria across 13 Principles but excluding the higher-ambition progress criteria for sourcing and decarbonisation.
comet-rs:CorporateOwner: The parent company that owns one or more ResponsibleSteel certified steelmaking sites and is accountable for group-level commitments, climate transition plans, and policy compliance under Principle 1.
comet-rs:CrudeSteelIntensity: A steelmaking site's greenhouse gas emissions expressed in tonnes of CO2 equivalent per tonne of crude steel produced, covering Scope 1, Scope 2, and upstream Scope 3 emissions from raw material to first solidification.
comet-rs:DPLThreshold: The mathematical boundary parameters — a y-intercept and a slope — that define each of the four Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) tiers, combining a site's emissions intensity and scrap input share into a single pass/fail test.
comet-rs:DRI_EAF: A lower-carbon steelmaking route using direct reduced iron (DRI) fed into an electric arc furnace (EAF), which can use green hydrogen instead of coal and is considered a key pathway to near-zero steel.
comet-rs:DecarbProgressLevel: A four-tier performance rating (DPL 1 to DPL 4) that grades a ResponsibleSteel site's decarbonisation progress based on its emissions intensity and scrap share; DPL 4 represents near-zero emissions.
comet-rs:EAF: An electric arc furnace (EAF), a steelmaking vessel that melts scrap or direct reduced iron using electricity rather than coal, enabling lower-carbon steel production when powered by clean energy.
comet-rs:EndOfLifeScrap: Post-consumer steel scrap collected after a product's useful life — such as demolished buildings or scrapped vehicles — counted in the scrap share calculation for Decarbonisation Progress Level assessment.
comet-rs:EnergyRecoveryCredit: A credit reducing a steelmaking site's reported emissions intensity for power and steam generated from captured process gases and waste heat, calculated using the IEA global grid intensity factor.
comet-rs:GreenSteelPremium: The price premium, in dollars or euros per tonne, that buyers pay for ResponsibleSteel certified low-carbon steel above the commodity market price for equivalent conventional steel.
comet-rs:HomeScrap: Pre-consumer scrap generated by steel product manufacturers outside the steelmaking site — such as stamping offcuts — and counted in the scrap share calculation for Decarbonisation Progress Level assessment.
comet-rs:InternalScrap: Steel scrap generated and re-melted within the same steelmaking process, excluded from the scrap share calculation because it never leaves the production boundary.
comet-rs:ManufacturingScrap: Steel scrap arising from downstream forming and fabrication operations — sometimes called prompt scrap — included in the scrap share calculation for Decarbonisation Progress Level assessment.
comet-rs:NonConformity: A finding during a ResponsibleSteel audit where a site does not meet a required criterion. Major non-conformities block certification; minor ones must be corrected but do not prevent it.
comet-rs:P01_CorporateLeadership: ResponsibleSteel Principle 1 — the requirement for a site's parent company to demonstrate visible, accountable corporate commitment to responsible steel production and continuous improvement.
comet-rs:P02_ESGManagementSystems: ResponsibleSteel Principle 2 — the requirement for a site to have documented environmental, social, and governance (ESG) management systems that identify risks and drive performance improvement.
comet-rs:P03_ResponsibleSourcing: ResponsibleSteel Principle 3 — the requirement for a site to know and manage the social and environmental risks in its upstream supply chain for key input materials such as iron ore and coal.
comet-rs:P04_Decommissioning: ResponsibleSteel Principle 4 — the requirement for a site to have a plan for safely closing, remediating, and rehabilitating the facility at the end of its operational life.
comet-rs:P05_OccupationalHealthSafety: ResponsibleSteel Principle 5 — the requirement for a site to systematically manage workplace health and safety risks to protect workers from injury and occupational illness.
comet-rs:P06_LabourRights: ResponsibleSteel Principle 6 — the requirement for a site to respect workers' rights including freedom of association, collective bargaining, fair pay, and prohibition of forced and child labour.
comet-rs:P07_HumanRights: ResponsibleSteel Principle 7 — the requirement for a site to identify, prevent, and remedy adverse human rights impacts connected to its operations, including on local and indigenous communities.
comet-rs:P08_StakeholderEngagement: ResponsibleSteel Principle 8 — the requirement for a site to engage meaningfully with affected stakeholders, disclose performance information, and respond to grievances.
comet-rs:P09_LocalCommunities: ResponsibleSteel Principle 9 — the requirement for a site to manage its impacts on neighbouring communities, including noise, dust, and traffic, and to contribute positively to local development.
comet-rs:P10_ClimateGHG: ResponsibleSteel Principle 10 — the requirement for a site to measure, report, and reduce its greenhouse gas emissions, including the Progress criteria that determine a site's Decarbonisation Progress Level rating.
comet-rs:P11_NoiseEmissionsWaste: ResponsibleSteel Principle 11 — the requirement for a site to identify, measure, and continuously reduce its air emissions, liquid effluents, solid waste, and noise impacts on the surrounding environment.
comet-rs:P12_WaterStewardship: Principle 12 of the ResponsibleSteel standard, requiring a steel production site to manage its water use, quality, and discharge responsibly.
comet-rs:P13_Biodiversity: Principle 13 of the ResponsibleSteel standard, requiring a steel site to assess and reduce its impacts on local ecosystems and wildlife.
comet-rs:PrincipleConformity: A pass/fail conformity result for one of the 13 ResponsibleSteel environmental and social principles assessed during a site audit.
comet-rs:ProcessGasBaseline: The greenhouse gas emissions (CO₂e) that would have occurred if steelmaking off-gases (e.g. blast furnace gas) had been flared rather than captured and used.
comet-rs:ProgressLevelPricing: The market price premium or discount tied to a steel site's Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL); higher DPL tiers attract larger green-steel premiums.
comet-rs:RSInputMaterial: Any raw material or fuel fed into a steelmaking process and classified under ResponsibleSteel Annex 1, including scrap, pig iron, alloys, and energy fuels.
comet-rs:RSPrinciple: One of the 13 environmental, social, and governance principles that define the ResponsibleSteel International Production Standard.
comet-rs:RSSupplierTier: A supplier relationship classified by how well the steel site knows its raw-material suppliers, from basic region knowledge (tier 1) to full site-level due diligence.
comet-rs:RecognisedProgramme: A third-party audit or certification scheme (e.g. a mining standard) that ResponsibleSteel accepts as evidence of responsible raw-material sourcing.
comet-rs:SR_BOF: A steelmaking route that uses smelting reduction (SR) upstream of a basic oxygen furnace (BOF) to convert iron ore directly without a traditional blast furnace.
comet-rs:ScrapCategory: Classification of steel scrap by origin: internal process offcuts (excluded from the count), pre-consumer manufacturing scrap, or post-consumer end-of-life scrap.
comet-rs:ScrapShareCalculation: The formula that calculates what percentage of total metallic inputs at a steel site comes from recycled scrap, a key input for determining the site's DPL tier.
comet-rs:SourcingProgressLevel: A four-tier rating (SPL 1–4) of how rigorously a steel site tracks and assesses the environmental and social performance of its raw-material suppliers.
comet-rs:SteelCertification: A ResponsibleSteel certification that allows a site to market steel products with the RS Certified Steel mark, covering both core ESG criteria and decarbonisation progress.
comet-rs:SteelProductionRoute: The primary technology pathway used to make steel (e.g. blast furnace, electric arc furnace), which determines the applicable emission factors and DPL thresholds.
comet-rs:SupplierESGRisk: A structured assessment of a raw-material supplier's environmental, social, and governance risks against the 13 ResponsibleSteel principles.
comet-rs:TransitionPlanReview: An annual check that a steel site's climate transition plan remains aligned with Paris Agreement trajectories, including near-term targets and technology milestones.
comet-rs:ambitionGapDelta: The numeric difference (in tonnes CO₂e per tonne of steel) between a site's published decarbonisation target and its actual greenhouse gas intensity in the reporting year.
comet-rs:annualCrudeSteelProduction: Total saleable crude steel output in tonnes during the reporting year; used as the denominator when calculating a site's greenhouse gas intensity.
comet-rs:applicableDPL: Links a green-steel pricing signal to the specific Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) tier that triggers it.
comet-rs:auditedSite: Identifies which certified steel site a particular ResponsibleSteel certification audit covers.
comet-rs:certificateId: The unique alphanumeric code assigned to a ResponsibleSteel-certified site and printed on its official certification mark.
comet-rs:claimDPLContext: An inferred link that carries a site's Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) forward to any chain-of-custody claim traceable to that site's steel certification.
comet-rs:cocModel: Indicates whether certified steel is tracked through the supply chain by strict physical separation ('segregation') or by accounting credit ('mass-balance').
comet-rs:dplLevel: An integer from 1 to 4 representing a steel site's Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL), where 1 is entry-level and 4 is near-zero emissions.
comet-rs:dplThresholdB: The y-intercept constant in the linear equation that defines the boundary between two Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) tiers on the scrap-share vs. GHG intensity chart.
comet-rs:dplThresholdM: The slope constant in the linear equation that defines the DPL tier boundary; combined with the y-intercept it sets the minimum GHG performance required at each scrap-share level.
comet-rs:ghgIntensityValue: A site's total greenhouse gas emissions divided by crude steel output, expressed in tonnes CO₂e per tonne of steel.
comet-rs:hasDPL: Links a ResponsibleSteel steel certification to the Decarbonisation Progress Level (DPL) the site has achieved.
comet-rs:hasNonConformity: Links a certification audit to one or more findings where the site failed to meet a ResponsibleSteel requirement.
comet-rs:hasSPL: Links a ResponsibleSteel steel certification to the Materials Sourcing Progress Level (SPL) the site has achieved.
comet-rs:includesGHGScope: Identifies which GHG Protocol emission scopes (1, 2, and/or 3) are included within a site's reported greenhouse gas intensity calculation boundary.
comet-rs:materialOriginRegion: The geographic region of the country where a raw-material supplier is located; the minimum sourcing information required at ResponsibleSteel Progress Level 1.
comet-rs:metallicFraction: The proportion of pure iron in a steelmaking input material (e.g. 0.98 for scrap, 0.94 for direct reduced iron), used to weight inputs in the scrap share formula.
comet-rs:nonConformitySeverity: Indicates whether an audit finding is 'major' (blocks certification until fixed) or 'minor' (must be corrected but does not prevent certification).
comet-rs:panelDecision: The formal verdict of the ResponsibleSteel Assurance Panel after reviewing an audit: approve, conditional approval, or reject.
comet-rs:premiumCurrency: The ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. USD, EUR) for the green-steel price premium associated with a ResponsibleSteel certification tier.
comet-rs:premiumPerTonne: The monetary premium paid per tonne of certified green steel, reflecting the market value of a site's ResponsibleSteel certification tier.
comet-rs:primarySecondaryClassification: Labels a steelmaking input as either 'primary' (virgin iron sources like pig iron or DRI) or 'secondary' (recycled scrap) for use in the scrap share formula.
comet-rs:principleAssessed: Links a conformity result to the specific one of the 13 ResponsibleSteel principles being evaluated.
comet-rs:processGasPowerMWh: Electricity generated from recovered steelmaking off-gases (e.g. coke oven gas), recorded in megawatt-hours for the energy-recovery credit calculation.
comet-rs:productionRoute: Links a steel site record to its primary steelmaking technology pathway, determining applicable emission benchmarks and DPL thresholds.
comet-rs:reviewsAudit: Links an Assurance Panel review to the specific certification audit being evaluated.
comet-rs:scrapSharePercent: The percentage of total metallic inputs that consists of recycled steel scrap; a key determinant of a site's Decarbonisation Progress Level tier.
comet-rs:siteAuditBoundary: A text description of the physical facilities and operations included within the scope of a ResponsibleSteel certification audit.
comet-rs:splLevel: An integer from 1 to 4 representing the Materials Sourcing Progress Level (SPL); higher numbers indicate more rigorous supplier due diligence.
comet-rs:traceableTo: Links a chain-of-custody claim made by a downstream buyer back to the originating ResponsibleSteel steel certification at the producing site.
comet-rs:transferQuantityTonnes: The weight of certified steel transferred between two parties in a single chain-of-custody handover event, recorded in tonnes.
comet-rs:transfersFrom: Identifies the organisation (seller or producer) that hands over certified steel in a chain-of-custody transfer event.
comet-rs:transfersTo: Identifies the organisation (buyer or processor) that receives certified steel in a chain-of-custody transfer event.
comet-rs:transitionPlanReviewDate: The calendar date on which a steel site's climate transition plan was most recently reviewed against its decarbonisation pathway.
comet-rs:upstreamPowerConsumptionMWh: Electricity consumed by upstream steelmaking processes (before the crude steel gate), used to calculate the net energy-recovery credit.
comet-rs:wasteEnergyPowerMWh: Electricity generated from residual waste heat or other by-product energy streams at a steel site, recorded in megawatt-hours for the energy-recovery credit.
comet-sc:ActivityDataRecord: A measured quantity of a business activity (e.g. fuel burned, kilometres driven) that is multiplied by an emission factor to estimate greenhouse gas emissions.
comet-sc:BaseYearEmissions: The historical greenhouse gas inventory for a chosen reference year, used as the baseline against which future reduction targets and progress are measured.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator: A five-dimension score evaluating the reliability of the data used in a greenhouse gas calculation, covering coverage, geography, reliability, technology, and time period.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator.coverageDQ: The share (0–100%) of a company's activities covered by directly measured primary data rather than estimates or averages.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator.geographyD: A score (1–3) indicating how closely the geographic origin of an emission factor matches the actual location of the activity being measured.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator.reliabilit: A score (1–3) indicating how trustworthy the data source is, ranging from verified primary measurements to unverified estimates.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator.technology: A score (1–3) indicating how closely the technology assumed in the emission factor matches the actual process generating the emissions.
comet-sc:DataQualityIndicator.temporalit: A score (1–3) indicating how recently the emission factor data was collected; fresher data scores higher.
comet-sc:EmissionIntensity: Greenhouse gas emissions normalised by a unit of output or revenue (e.g. tonnes CO₂e per tonne of product), used to compare performance across sites or time.
comet-sc:PrimaryData: Activity data measured directly at the source (e.g. fuel meter readings, supplier-specific emission factors) rather than derived from industry averages.
comet-sc:PrimaryDataShare: The percentage of a company's total greenhouse gas footprint calculated using directly measured primary data rather than secondary estimates.
comet-sc:RecalculationTrigger: A significant structural or methodological change (e.g. an acquisition or new calculation standard) that requires the historical base-year emissions to be recalculated.
comet-sc:Scope1Emissions: Direct greenhouse gas emissions from sources owned or controlled by the reporting company, such as on-site combustion and industrial processes.
comet-sc:Scope2Emissions: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity or heat, reported both on a location-based grid-average basis and a market-based (contract-specific) basis.
comet-sc:Scope3Emissions: All other indirect greenhouse gas emissions across a company's value chain, from raw-material extraction through product use and disposal, split across 15 standard categories.
comet-sc:Scope3Emissions.category: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 category number (1–15) identifying which part of the value chain the indirect emissions come from.
comet-sc:SpendProxy: A low-accuracy Scope 3 estimate derived by multiplying supplier spend by an economy-wide emission intensity factor, used when no activity data is available.
comet-sc:SupplyChainLink: A recorded relationship between a buyer and a specific supplier, enabling traceability of emissions through the upstream supply chain.
comet-sc:TransportEvent: A single logistics movement record capturing mode of transport, distance, weight, and the resulting freight emissions.
comet-sc:category: The integer (1–15) identifying which GHG Protocol Scope 3 category a set of indirect value-chain emissions belongs to.
comet-tfs:AR1: The IPCC First Assessment Report (1990) set of global warming potential (GWP) values; a selectable characterization factor version in the TfS product carbon footprint model.
comet-tfs:AR2: The IPCC Second Assessment Report (1995) set of global warming potential (GWP) values; a selectable characterization factor version in the TfS product carbon footprint model.
comet-tfs:AR3: The IPCC Third Assessment Report (2001) set of global warming potential (GWP) values; a selectable characterization factor version in the TfS product carbon footprint model.
comet-tfs:AR4: The IPCC Fourth Assessment Report (2007) set of global warming potential (GWP) values; a selectable characterization factor version in the TfS product carbon footprint model.
comet-tfs:AR5: The IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (2013) set of global warming potential (GWP) values; a selectable characterization factor version in the TfS product carbon footprint model.
comet-tfs:AR6: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (2021) global warming potential (GWP) values; the default and most current version used in TfS product carbon footprint (PCF) calculations.
comet-tfs:AT_FirstParty: A product carbon footprint (PCF) self-attestation by the supplier itself, with no independent external review; the lowest trust level in the TfS attestation hierarchy.
comet-tfs:AT_MassBalanceCertificate: A chain-of-custody certificate confirming that a specified quantity of sustainable or low-carbon material has been accounted for via a mass-balance scheme.
comet-tfs:AT_ProgramCertification: A product carbon footprint (PCF) certified under an accredited programme with full third-party audit; the highest trust level in the TfS attestation hierarchy.
comet-tfs:AT_SecondParty: A product carbon footprint (PCF) review conducted by a customer or industry association rather than an independent auditor; an intermediate trust level.
comet-tfs:AT_ThirdParty: A product carbon footprint (PCF) independently verified by an accredited external auditor; a high trust level in the TfS attestation framework.
comet-tfs:AllocationApproach: A record of how a supplier has allocated shared process emissions across co-products, waste incineration, material recycling, and carbon capture and utilisation (CCU).
comet-tfs:AttestationOfConformance: A formal declaration attached to a product carbon footprint (PCF) record that identifies who verified the PCF, under which standard, and to what level of assurance.
comet-tfs:AttestationType: A picklist specifying the level of trust associated with a PCF attestation, from self-declaration (1st party) through programme certification.
comet-tfs:CCUCalculationApproach: The method used to account for carbon captured and utilised (CCU) in a product carbon footprint (PCF): not applicable, cut-off (ignore), or credit (allocate benefit).
comet-tfs:CCU_CreditMethod: A carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) accounting option that allocates a credit to the product for the CO₂ it temporarily or permanently stores.
comet-tfs:CCU_CutOffMethod: A carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) accounting option that ignores any carbon storage benefit; the captured CO₂ is treated as if it were emitted.
comet-tfs:CCU_NotApplicable: Indicates that carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) is not part of the production process and no CCU accounting adjustment is needed.
comet-tfs:CF_Unspecified: Indicates that the IPCC characterization factor version used for global warming potential (GWP) values has not been declared in the product carbon footprint record.
comet-tfs:CarbonContentBreakdown: A decomposition of a product's total carbon content into its fossil, biogenic, packaging, recycled, and CCU-based components, all expressed in kilograms of carbon per declared unit.
comet-tfs:CharacterizationFactor: The IPCC Assessment Report edition (e.g. AR5, AR6) whose global warming potential (GWP) multipliers are used to convert each greenhouse gas into CO₂-equivalent tonnes.
comet-tfs:CradleToGate: A partial product carbon footprint (PCF) scope that covers all emissions from raw-material extraction up to the point the product leaves the producer's factory gate.
comet-tfs:CradleToGrave: A full product carbon footprint (PCF) scope that covers all lifecycle emissions from raw-material extraction through the product's use and final disposal.
comet-tfs:CrossSectoralStandard: The overarching greenhouse gas accounting standard(s) the PCF calculation follows, such as the GHG Protocol or ISO 14067, as declared in the TfS data model.
comet-tfs:CutOffRule: The TfS rule permitting exclusion of up to 10% of total emissions from a product carbon footprint (PCF) when those emissions are judged too minor to justify measurement effort.
comet-tfs:DataModelVersion: The version identifier of the TfS PCF data model specification that an exchanged product carbon footprint record conforms to.
comet-tfs:DataQualityRating: The TfS data quality rating (DQR) block covering primary data share and three scored dimensions (technological, temporal, geographical match), each rated 1–5.
comet-tfs:DeclaredUnitOfMeasurement: The standard unit of analysis for a TfS product carbon footprint (PCF), chosen from an ISO unit code list (e.g. kg, litre, piece).
comet-tfs:DistributionStage: The life-cycle segment covering outbound logistics from the producer's gate to the customer's receiving point, with its own greenhouse gas emission breakdown.
comet-tfs:GWPPositionBreakdown: A structured decomposition of a life-cycle stage's global warming potential (GWP) into labelled positions: fossil, biogenic, land-use change, and aviation contributions.
comet-tfs:GeographyRegionOrSubregion: The ISO 3166 world region of a supplier's production site, used when a specific country is not disclosed in the TfS product carbon footprint record.
comet-tfs:LifeCycleStage: One of the three TfS life-cycle segments (Production, Packaging, Distribution) each carrying its own greenhouse gas emission breakdown for a product carbon footprint.
comet-tfs:MB_Both: A mass-balance calculation approach option that applies both the conventional reference method and the inventory method simultaneously to allocate sustainable feedstock credits.
comet-tfs:MB_ConventionalReference: A mass-balance approach that benchmarks the carbon footprint of a sustainable feedstock against a conventional fossil-based reference product to derive the credit.
comet-tfs:MB_Inventory: A mass-balance approach that tracks and accounts for the actual lifecycle inventory of the sustainable feedstock to derive the emission credit.
comet-tfs:MassBalanceCalculationApproach: The method chosen for calculating the carbon benefit of mass-balanced sustainable feedstocks: conventional reference, inventory-based, or both.
comet-tfs:MassBalancing: A TfS data block recording whether mass balancing (credit) is used, whether free attribution applies, the calculation approach, and the certification scheme (e.g. ISCC+).
comet-tfs:PackagingStage: The life-cycle segment that details greenhouse gas emissions attributable to product packaging; these emissions are also rolled into the Production Stage total.
comet-tfs:PartialFullPcf: Declares whether a product carbon footprint (PCF) is partial (cradle-to-gate only) or full (cradle-to-grave through end-of-life); TfS defaults to cradle-to-gate.
comet-tfs:PositiveListReference: A pointer to the TfS-published approved lists of product category rules (PCRs) and substitution products accepted for use in PCF calculations.
comet-tfs:PostConsumer: Recycled material sourced from products that have been used and discarded by end consumers, such as household or commercial waste streams.
comet-tfs:PostIndustrial: Recycled material derived from manufacturing offcuts or rejects that never reached a consumer; also called pre-consumer scrap.
comet-tfs:ProductOrSectorRule: The most specific product category rule (PCR) or sector guideline applied in a TfS product carbon footprint calculation, defaulting to the TfS PCF Guideline v3.0.
comet-tfs:ProductionStage: The cradle-to-gate life-cycle segment covering all emissions from raw-material extraction to the producer's factory gate, including packaging if that flag is set.
comet-tfs:RC_CutOff: A recycled-material accounting option that assigns zero emission burden to recycled inputs; the upstream production impact of the original material is ignored.
comet-tfs:RC_UpstreamSystemExpansion: A recycled-material accounting option that credits the product for displacing the need to produce virgin material, reducing its net carbon footprint.
comet-tfs:RecycledCarbonAllocation: The method used to account for recycled material in a product carbon footprint (PCF): cut-off (zero burden) or upstream system expansion (displacement credit).
comet-tfs:RecycledContentType: Declares whether recycled inputs in a product came from post-industrial manufacturing waste or from post-consumer end-of-life material.
comet-tfs:Region_Africa: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown representing the African continent, used when a specific country is not disclosed.
comet-tfs:Region_Americas: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown representing North and South America combined, used when a specific country is not disclosed.
comet-tfs:Region_Asia: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown representing the Asian continent, used when a specific country is not disclosed.
comet-tfs:Region_AustraliaNewZealand: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown representing Australia and New Zealand, used when a specific country is not disclosed.
comet-tfs:Region_CentralAsia: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering Central Asian countries such as Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
comet-tfs:Region_EasternAsia: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering Eastern Asian countries such as China, Japan, and South Korea.
comet-tfs:Region_EasternEurope: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering Eastern European countries such as Poland and Romania.
comet-tfs:Region_Europe: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown representing the European continent, used when a specific country is not disclosed.
comet-tfs:Region_Global: A geographic region option in the TfS supplier location dropdown indicating the supplier draws from or operates across the entire world.
comet-tfs:Region_LatinAmericaCaribbean: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering Latin America and Caribbean countries.
comet-tfs:Region_Melanesia: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering the Melanesian Pacific island group (e.g. Papua New Guinea, Fiji).
comet-tfs:Region_Micronesia: A geographic subregion option in the TfS supplier location dropdown covering the Micronesian Pacific island group (e.g. Guam, Palau).
